_comment: Mutation testing (Phase 2). Line coverage says a line RAN; a mutation score says a test would NOTICE if that line were wrong. The unit tier sits at 92.57% lines, and the three data-loss defects the property tests found (CHECKPOINT.md §6a) were all in code that was already 'covered' -- which is exactly the gap this measures. Run with `npm run test:mutation`.
_comment_vitest: related:false is required, not tuning. Stryker's default asks vitest for the test files 'related' to a mutated source file; that graph comes up empty in this repo (imports carry explicit .ts extensions, a repo convention -- see CLAUDE.md), so the dry run aborts with 'No tests were executed'. Running the whole tier is affordable: it is ~1.3s.
_comment_thresholds: Measured baseline at the commit that added this file: 70.66% overall (2123 mutants; 1285 killed, 13 timeout, 398 survived, 141 with no coverage). `break` ratchets: it is raised to just under the measured score each time a batch of tests lands, never set ahead of the work (setting the 85% target up front would fail every PR for the duration). History: 65 (baseline 70.66) -> 73 (measured 75.12) -> 75 (measured 77.58, after the five-lane merge added the logger and privacy modules, both of which arrived with their own tests) -> 80 (measured 80.31, after 27 storage tests took storage/** from 64.09 to 84.52). Target floor is 85 per the user. The gap below the measured score leaves room for the 13 timeout-classified mutants, the one non-deterministic part of the score. Never lower it.
